claims.text: Introducing a heterogeneous lamella structure into eutectic high-entropy alloys increases strength relative to alloys without that structure.
Introducing a heterogeneous lamella structure into eutectic high-entropy alloys increases ductility relative to alloys without that structure.
A heterogeneous lamella structure combines ultrafine-grain strengthening with coarse-grain ductility.
Combining hard and soft domains in a heterogeneous lamellar structure produces internal back stresses that can contribute to simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement should hold at room temperature and ambient pressure.
Maintaining alloy stability is a necessary condition for the heterogeneous lamella intervention to work.
The exact mechanism responsible for the proposed strength-ductility enhancement is not fully understood.
Coherent nanoscale internal boundaries or interfaces can strengthen metals.
